headline: AI‑enhanced malware automates victim profiling for faster credential theft
dek: Cisco Talos reports Volta‑Autodoxer embeds a large language model to analyze stolen data and rank victim value, speeding up attacks[S1].
what_happened: Volta-Autodoxer uses an LLM to automatically profile and prioritize stolen credentials for attackers[S1].
Apple CEO John Ternus says AI will be used selectively, aiming for products people love rather than AI for AI’s sake[S2].
Pika H3 Flex creates synchronized video and stereo audio in six steps, handling up to 12 references[S3].

sections.title: Volta-autodoxer adds AI to infostealer malware
paragraphs: Cisco Talos researchers disclosed a new strain of infostealer malware called Volta-Autodoxer that incorporates large language model (LLM) functionality to profile victims and prioritize high‑value data[S1]. The malware automatically gathers credentials, tokens and payment information before sending a serialized dossier to an LLM for analysis[S1].

Volta-Autodoxer collects passwords, browser‑saved credentials, Microsoft OAuth tokens, cookies, payment cards and crypto‑wallet seed phrases, as well as active sessions on Discord, Telegram, Steam and Roblox[S1]. After the initial sweep it performs a deeper scan of central accounts such as Gmail, extracting receipts, order history and location data from services like UberEats[S1].

Infostealer malware has long been used to harvest login details that fuel large data breaches, including incidents involving Snowflake, AT&T, Ticketmaster and Disney[S1]. Cisco Talos flagged the tool using its new CAIRN framework, which detects hacking tools that embed AI capabilities, though the researchers have not observed active deployments in the wild[S1].

sections.title: Apple CEO on AI strategy
paragraphs: Apple CEO John Ternus said the company will use artificial intelligence in upcoming devices, but it will not release AI features just for their own sake[S2]. He became CEO in September and addressed the topic in a Wired interview with Steven Levy[S2]. Ternus emphasized that the goal is to create products people love, regardless of whether AI is involved[S2].

Ternus noted that Apple has been perceived as lagging because Siri’s more powerful version only arrived this summer[S2]. He argued that when AI is applied correctly, users should not need to consider the underlying technology[S2]. He also said that AI could eventually make tasks like app creation easier, but product creation remains a human‑driven activity[S2].

The CEO’s comments come as the industry debates whether AI agents might replace traditional apps[S2]. Ternus’ stance suggests Apple will continue to prioritize user experience over showcasing AI for its own novelty[S2].

card.hook: Apple will only ship AI when it adds clear user value[S2].
points: Apple delayed a stronger Siri until summer 2026[S2].
CEO John Ternus became chief in September 2026[S2].
AI should be invisible to users if done right[S2].

sections.title: Pika H3 Flex video‑audio model architecture
paragraphs: Pika Labs released Pika H3 Flex, a post‑trained H3 model for professional creators, on 29 October 2026[S3]. The model generates video with synchronized stereo audio in six sampling steps[S3]. It supports up to 12 reference inputs and can produce native 480p or 768p video locally, with higher resolutions via the hosted API[S3].

The architecture adds two task adapters: FL2VA for text and endpoint‑frame conditioning, and Ref2VA for multimodal references[S3]. It builds on the MiniMax‑H3 base model and processes prompts and media through an encoder before producing video and audio latents[S3]. The inference pipeline then decodes these latents and combines them into an MP4 file, automatically downloading the pinned base components and selected adapter[S3].
Pika H3 Flex integrates both modalities, allowing creators to control motion and sound together, which simplifies multi‑shot storytelling and motion‑graphics workflows[S3].

points: Six sampling steps produce video and audio together[S3].
Two adapters handle text and multimodal references[S3].

sections.title: OpenAI lowers funding target to $20 billion
paragraphs: OpenAI announced that it has reduced the size of its upcoming financing round to a $20 billion target after earlier reports of a $30 billion raise[S5]. The revision follows a valuation drop from $1.4 trillion to $1.25 trillion and comes ahead of a planned initial public offering[S5]. Investors from the United Arab Emirates will lead the round, with a possible retail tranche for wealthy individuals[S5].

The company has already secured $11 billion in commitments, according to a Wall Street Journal follow‑up, but the overall response from large investors has been described as “tepid”[S5]. The first close of the round is expected to be below the $20 billion goal, and the total may only be reached through the additional retail offering[S5]. Analysts suggest that the softer fundraising environment is linked to Wall Street’s caution over heavy AI infrastructure spending and a broader sell‑off in tech stocks[S5].

sections.title: AI agent performs brain injection on live mouse
paragraphs: Biotech founder Gabriel Ocana Santero connected an AI agent to a robotic arm, injector and camera to perform a brain injection on a living mouse[S6]. The experiment was carried out by his company Exin Therapeutics in San Francisco and was reported on 31 October 2026[S6]. The AI chose a therapy from 19 options, set injection coordinates and controlled the needle during the procedure[S6].

The setup included a motorized device to immobilize the mouse, a camera for visual feedback and a robotic injector that the AI could move[S6]. The team first tried Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5, which refused to guide the needle, citing internal safety warnings[S6]. They switched to Claude Sonnet 5, which completed the injection as instructed[S6].

AI models used in research are typically trained on published papers, so they miss real‑time observations and failed experiments[S6]. By giving an AI direct control of lab hardware, researchers hope to make models more reliable and useful for experimental design[S6]. Santero’s test shows both the promise and the current safety limits of such integration[S6].

card.hook: AI completed a live mouse brain injection[S6].
points: 19 therapy options were evaluated by the AI[S6].
Claude Opus 5.5 refused to inject, citing safety[S6].
Claude Sonnet 5 performed the injection successfully[S6].

why_it_matters.text: The AI‑driven profiling could let cybercriminals prioritize high‑value accounts more quickly, increasing the risk of large‑scale data breaches for individuals and businesses that store credentials, payment info, and crypto wallets[S1].

OpenAI’s reduced $20 billion funding round reflects investor caution about costly AI infrastructure, which may slow the pace of new AI tools and affect market dynamics for companies relying on large‑scale models[S5].
